_what: What the index coverage probe in scripts/db/run.mjs reads (ERD §3.3, docs/sprint-0a/sprint-0a-core-erd-rls-retention-th.md:109: every FK, RLS predicate and keyset cursor column has an index; the FK half is the FK support probe). Rule 1 is computed live, not listed: every column of a table in app or private that a policy on that table reads in its USING half (a pg_depend dependency of the policy whose name the USING deparse carries unqualified or qualified by the table) must sit in the leading run of some valid whole BTREE index on that table whose key columns are all USING columns of the table, or be exempt here by schema.table.column with a reason. Rule 2: every lookup below is served by a valid BTREE index whose key columns BEGIN with its columns in order, direction and NULLS order included (a column here carries NULLS FIRST or NULLS LAST only where it differs from its direction's default; none does), and whose predicate is the lookup's where (or none). Rule 3: every exemption names a column rule 1 reads and finds uncovered, so an exemption cannot outlive its reason. Both rules read the access method and rule 2 the NULLS order since batch 150-prereq's review round (C0-1, Q0 Q-1: a HASH, a BRIN and a DESC NULLS LAST rebuild each passed every layer while the declared query lost its index). A green lookup says an index of that shape exists, not that the query plans through it: the workspace switch / list lookup is green while the WS:913 workspace list seq-scans app.workspaces (F2, open_blockers[194] (1)).
_measured: On a clean migrate-clean at 1319042: 112 (table, column) pairs read by a USING half, 108 covered, the 4 below uncovered; 28 lookups, all served. The lookups are the six named queries of WS:909-917 the existing indexes serve, plus every index the migrations named *_keyset_idx, plus the two the survey and the metering batch name.

findings.query: parent lookups inside a USING subquery
findings.finding: Rule 1 reads the policy's OWN table. The EXISTS subqueries of the 33 scope narrowings look up their parent by (workspace_id, business_profile_id, id), which each parent's scope key carries today; no rule reads that, and a parent rebuilt without its scope key would be named only by the FK support probe if a key references it.
